found.notes: DEBT raised by a special-purpose vehicle (the LESSOR), not by Anthropic: the SPV raises debt plus equity, buys Google TPUs (co-designed with Broadcom) and leases them to Anthropic; lease payments service the notes. Per Bloomberg (via Investing.com, 2026-06-05): A1 notes $6B priced ~T+100bp, A2 notes $24B at a 5.75% coupon, B notes $4.5B at 8.5%; senior tranches rated investment grade (private ratings); Broadcom gives residual-value support covering any shortfall for A1/A2 holders if Anthropic defaults and recovered chips sell for less than owed; roughly half syndicated to outside investors (insurers incl. Apollo's Athene, banks). Arrangers: Wells Fargo (global coordinator), BNP Paribas, Citi, UBS; A2 placement agents Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, Morgan Stanley (Yahoo pricing story). The first Bloomberg report (2026-05-28/29) had about $36B with A2 at $25B; the final is about $35B. FT (2026-08-03, via The Decoder and heise) describes the vehicle as 'Compute SPV' which bought about 1M TPUs for $35B, with a Broadcom backstop of about $30B; Google separately backstops data-center leases (10 projects, 2.4 GW; up to $44B exposure, $815M recorded), which is a different instrument. Anthropic is the lessee/obligor on the lease, not the issuer of these notes. The claim label '(lessor debt; not Anthropic-issued)' is correct; it must be excluded from Anthropic's own capital raised. FOLLOW-ON DEALS (see follow_on_spv_deals_not_confirmed_closed): by 2026-09-30 I found NO report that a second chip-lease SPV deal had closed, so the closed, priced amount is the June $35B only; if the draft's figure is about $71B it adds a preliminary, unclosed deal.
